headline: All majors below 200-day lines in extreme fear, but whale accumulation and stablecoin moves suggest a structural bid beneath the tape.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguously bearish across the board. Bitcoin trades 48.4% below its 12-month high at 64,345, Ethereum 61% underwater at 1,877, and every major asset sits below its 200-day simple moving average with no golden crosses in place. The combined picture is one of sustained downtrend with no technical recovery signal in the near structure. That said, the momentum readings are not uniformly weak: Bitcoin's RSI sits neutral at 51.8, Ethereum at 52.3, and both have MACD below signal line, which is the expected posture in a downtrend. The real outlier is BNB, which shows RSI of 59.5 with MACD above signal (the only major to post that combination), suggesting a localized rebound against the broader weakness. ADA is more extreme: RSI at 67.7 with MACD above signal and a 7-day gain of 17.3%, a rare pocket of momentum in a sea of lethargy. The rest of the majors languish: SOL's RSI at 48, XRP's at 46.5, DOGE at 43.6, all below midline and all with MACD below signal. This is not a market testing its lows; it is a market sitting on them.

Positioning in derivatives tells a clearer story than price action alone. Bitcoin funding is trivial at 0.07% annualized, a sign that carry trades are not crowded or expensive to hold, which usually means room to move either way without immediate pain. Ethereum is inverted: funding is negative at minus 4.4% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs, a signal that the short side is overextended or that leverage has swung against bears. Yet the open interest remains substantial: Bitcoin at 2.01 billion USD, Ethereum at 1.34 billion. The long-to-short ratios are notably skewed toward longs (Bitcoin 1.35 to 1, Ethereum 1.74 to 1, SOL 2.55 to 1), a crowded bet on the long side in a downtrend. In the last 24 hours, liquidations have been brutal for longs: Bitcoin saw 1.41 million liquidated against 4.23 million on shorts, a 3-to-1 imbalance favoring the short side. Ethereum liquidated 2.72 million longs against 5.15 million shorts, again a net win for bears. This is the tape of a market wringing out leverage in both directions, but with longs taking more pain.

Whale behavior and stablecoin float paint a tension worth naming. Over the past 24 hours, 239.6 million USD moved off exchanges net, with Bitcoin accounting for 185.9 million and Ethereum for 53.8 million. This is accumulation: large accounts moving coins to cold storage or self-custody. That same window saw 174.8 million USDT move off OKEx and 120 million USDC move off Coinbase Institutional, also off exchanges. But the biggest stablecoin moves worked in the opposite direction: 119.9 million USDC moved onto Coinbase Institutional and 102.8 million USDT onto Bitfinex. The net result is a 72.1 million USD loss in stablecoin buying power, dry powder consumed. Over a longer frame, the weekly trends show the key inflection: two weeks ago, weekly net was minus 225 million and minus 218 million (inflow bias), but the last two weeks flipped decisively, posting plus 1.01 billion and plus 1.20 billion outflow (accumulation bias). This is the pattern of institutions and whales stepping in as fear peaks.

Crowd sentiment is parked at extreme fear, with the Fear & Greed index at 25 on a 30-day range of 20 to 33, near the bottom of the recent band. This is the emotional floor. Meanwhile, the tape shows that traditional finance (US spot ETF flows) is fractured: Bitcoin ETFs posted 170.1 million inflow on August 3, but only one day of same-direction flow in the last five sessions, with the five-day net a modest 120.2 million. Ethereum ETFs went the other way, minus 11.9 million on the latest print and minus 13.6 million over five sessions. The traditional bid is present for Bitcoin but thin and unstable for Ethereum. Total market cap grew 0.55% in 24 hours to 2.28 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance held firm at 56.6%, a sign that outflows are not fleeing to altcoins but instead off market entirely.

Watch two conditions closely. First, whether the negative Ethereum funding persists and whether long liquidations continue to exceed short liquidations across both major assets: a sustained regime of shorts being paid and longs being flushed would signal a structural shift to downside momentum. Second, track the weekly whale outflow trend: if the last two weeks' combined 2.21 billion in net outflows (accumulation) reverses back to inflows over the next one or two weeks, the marginal bid will have shifted. Finally, monitor whether Bitcoin and Ethereum can reclaim or even stabilize above their respective 50-day moving averages: the 200-day line is too far away to act as near-term resistance, but a 50-day recovery would be the first technical signal that the tape has changed its character.
